fields.description:
## Gap

batter-7r3.8 lets owned fixtures construct pools that authenticate as a separately provisioned login (PlannedPool::password_login). Session policy can only be applied through public native hooks (PgSessionProfile::reset_and_apply in after_connect/after_release). PgProfiledPool and RunledgerDatabase cannot host a fixture-managed pool, and PgProfiledPool's before_acquire verify_idle hook is crate-private, so a fixture pool cannot reproduce the application's full three-hook profiled pool or hand out a PgProfiledPool/RunledgerDatabase handle that the fixture driver closes.

## Direction

Let a planned fixture pool be declared with a PgSessionProfile so the fixture constructs it through PgProfiledPool::connect_lazy (all three hooks owned by the library, no replaceable setup callback) after login resolution, registers it before the first connectivity check, and closes it before lease cleanup. Compose with batter-nhu5's single profiled pool owner rather than adding a second one.

## Evidence

ADR-010 'Fixture login pool assessment (batter-7r3.8)'; bead comment 391 on batter-7r3.8 (consumer A's close-aware adapter).
fields.acceptance_criteria: A fixture-declared profiled pool (lease or password login) is constructed through the library-owned three-hook path, registered before the first connectivity check and closed before lease cleanup; live tests prove profile verification on acquisition and retained failures; no replaceable hook or second pool owner is introduced; bash scripts/verify.sh passes.
fields.title: Host profiled pools inside owned SQLx fixtures

data.text:
Implementation (commit 1a81076, branch feat/sqlx-fixture-connection-profiles-7r3-8). Design: ConnectionPlan::declare(reserved) -> PlanDeclaration::pool(PlannedPool) -> PoolKey; FixtureDatabase::pool / DatabaseFixture::pool select by key and refuse another plan's key. PlannedPool::{lease_login, password_login(options, username, SecretString)}: a password login replaces only username/password on the lease's own parsed native options, so retargeting, half-replaced credentials and swapped passwords cannot be written (a proposed connect-options closure was rejected in a four-lens design review). Each lease URL must select lease.database_name(), else LeaseDatabaseMismatch inside sqlx::Error::Configuration before any pool exists (harness keeps the admin query; SQLx lets dbname override the path). Owned and low-level paths resolve, construct+register each pool, then check, so every declared pool is registered before the first connectivity check. No FixtureError variant or report field added; ConnectionPlan::new unchanged. Two adversarial review rounds (16 confirmed findings) applied. ADR-010 assessment recorded.

Verification (Linux, pinned Rust 1.98.1): bash scripts/verify.sh passed (fmt, file budgets, four Clippy configs, six test-matrix parts, rustdoc, five HTTP smokes). Live: bash scripts/test_reference_live.sh against two task-owned PostgreSQL 18.6 containers (SCRAM, autovacuum_naptime=1s, max_prepared_transactions=10): 72/72 cases (67 database probes incl. four new fixture_login_* cases) plus both library probes passed; baseline on the unchanged tree was 68/68. Mutations: reverting either path to per-pool construct-then-check fails its registration witness; a password login that keeps the owner's password fails all four new live cases and the unit test. Public API: rustdoc JSON surface.py (nightly) vs ae000c7: batter-sqlx 1315->1347 entries, 0 removed, 32 added (5 use entries are the non-cut plan submodule move); batter facade unchanged. Not run: MSRV 1.94 and macOS (CI-owned), separate SQLx live suite (scripts/test_sqlx_live.sh; untouched code), fresh-agent usability evaluation (proposed, unexecuted). Limitations: PgProfiledPool/RunledgerDatabase cannot host fixture pools (follow-up batter-7r3.8.1, related batter-nhu5); binding holds at pool construction only (set_connect_options escape hatch); role lifecycle stays caller-owned.

Started on branch feat/bulkhead-run-blocking-0772 (from origin/master d7fcc01). Running a design panel for Bulkhead::run_blocking before implementation.

Implemented Bulkhead::run_blocking + BlockingError (crates/batter-core/src/admission/blocking.rs). Design: 3-lens design panel + 3 judges; spec kept closure -> plain T, four-variant exhaustive error (NotAdmitted/NotStarted/Abandoned/Panicked), no From impls, post-grant context recheck, no abort, dispatcher+span coverage. Review round 1 (5 lenses, 2 skeptics each) confirmed: (high) work span closed outside captured dispatcher -> caller span leak or Registry panic turning success into Panicked; (medium) runtime without time driver panicked after handoff leaving a detached closure with its permit; missing first-poll dispatcher test; 4 doc wording fixes. All repaired with regression tests; mutation checks show each reverted repair fails exactly its new test(s). Full verify.sh running.

Verification (Linux, pinned Rust 1.98.1): bash scripts/verify.sh passed twice: on the round-1 repairs, and on the final code after the round-2 runtime-entry fix (exit 0; fmt, file budgets, four Clippy configurations, all six test-matrix parts, rustdoc, five HTTP smokes). Afterwards only comments/docs changed; cargo fmt --check, batter-core clippy -D warnings -D clippy::mod_module_files and RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc re-run clean. New coverage: 30 admission-target integration tests, 7 unit tests, 5 metrics tests, 1 redaction test, 1 runnable doctest, 2 compile-fail doctests; an implementation agent reran the admission target 60 extra times without flakes. Mutation checks: reverting each repair (span closed outside dispatcher, timer-driver probe, first-poll dispatch scope, runtime lookup order, result-wait runtime entry) fails exactly its new test(s). Review round 2 + skeptic: Wait call finished from another context could panic after handoff -> result wait now polled inside the first-poll runtime; documented that both deadline timers belong to that runtime (fire only while it is driven; panic if polled after it shut down) and that the cross-context reasoning is unverified under tokio_unstable alt timer. Limitations: MSRV 1.94 and macOS not run locally (CI); NotStarted covered at mapping level only; Tokio's OS-thread-refusal panic source-inspected only; fresh-agent usability evaluation proposed and unexecuted. AGENTS.md (root code map) and crates/batter-core/AGENTS.md (entrypoint + invariants) were updated deliberately. PR: https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/72 (commit 14fa6bd).

data.reason: Delivered in PR https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/72 (commit 14fa6bd): Bulkhead::run_blocking admits like enter, rechecks the context after a grant, records one decision and moves the permit into the blocking closure in the same poll; the permit is held until the closure returns or unwinds, even when the caller is cancelled, times out or is dropped. Exhaustive BlockingError {NotAdmitted, NotStarted, Abandoned, Panicked}, no From impls, redacted payload; closure value returned unconverted; dispatcher/span cover execution, unstarted destruction and span close; runtime and time driver checked before admission and the result wait kept in that runtime. Contracts, ADR-010 assessment, ADR-014 note, status/testing/references/CHANGELOG updated; verify.sh passed on Rust 1.98.1. Shutdown settlement stays on the ADR-014 watch list.
